hints: For each word you want the shortest root it starts with. If you read the word one letter at a time, when is the earliest moment you can stop?
Put the roots in a trie and mark root ends. For each word, walk the trie letter by letter; the first marked node you reach is the shortest root. If the path breaks first, keep the word as it is.

1. Insert every root into a trie, marking the last node of each root.
  2. Split the sentence on spaces.
  3. For each word walk the trie: if a letter has no child, stop and keep the word.
  4. If you land on a marked node after k letters, replace the word by its first k letters and stop.
  5. Join the results with single spaces.

approaches.name: Brute force
approaches.idea: For every word, check every root with startsWith and keep the shortest match.

approaches.name: Better
approaches.idea: Put roots in a hash set and test each prefix of the word from shortest to longest.

approaches.name: Optimal
approaches.idea: Trie of roots: one walk per word that stops at the first root end.

explain: Sample roots sun, star, st and sentence sunny stars stay bright. Walking sunny: s→u→n, and n is marked, so it becomes sun. Walking stars: s→t, and t is already marked by the root st, so we stop there and output st even though star also matches; stopping at the first mark is what gives the shortest root. stay also becomes st, and bright breaks at once (no b child) and stays the same. Result: sun st st bright. Edge case: a word shorter than every matching root is left unchanged.
recognize: 'Replace each word by the shortest root it begins with' → trie of roots, stop at the first end-of-root mark.
